# Seams

> A CLI framework that generates modular Rails engines. Seams gives a Rails
> application the architectural benefits of microservices — clear boundaries,
> independent testing, team autonomy — without the operational cost. You ship a
> single Rails app; you think in independent engines. Every generated file
> belongs to the host and is editable; nothing is hidden behind the gem.

Key facts for machine readers:

- Language: Ruby (>= 4.0). Runtime dependencies: rails (>= 7.1, < 9.0), thor.
- Entry point: the `bin/seams` CLI in a host app (installed by
  `bin/rails generate seams:install`), e.g. `bin/seams core`, `bin/seams auth`,
  `bin/seams engine <name>`, `bin/seams list`, `bin/seams remove <name>`.
- Canonical engines: core, auth, accounts, notifications, billing, teams,
  admin, permissions, design — generated under the host's `engines/` directory.
- Engines communicate through events (`Seams::Events::Publisher`), never by
  calling each other's models directly; custom RuboCop cops enforce the
  boundaries (`lib/seams/cops/`).
- The gem materialises the patterns in the book "Modular Rails: Architecture
  for the Long Game" (https://davidslv.uk/modular-rails/); the
  seams-example repo (https://github.com/Davidslv/seams-example) is a
  reference host wiring every canonical engine.

## Documentation

- [Documentation site](https://davidslv.github.io/seams/): all guides, searchable, grouped by Diátaxis.
- [README](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/README.md): overview, quick start, the engine list.
- [Getting Started](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/tutorials/GETTING_STARTED.md): from `bundle install` to a booting host.
- [Tutorial](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/tutorials/TUTORIAL.md): a longer guided build.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/explanation/ARCHITECTURE.md): the model, and why events, boundary cops, and adapters.
- [Engine catalogue](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/reference/ENGINE_CATALOGUE.md): every canonical engine and what it owns.
- [Adding an engine](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/how-to/ADDING_AN_ENGINE.md) / [Removing an engine](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/how-to/REMOVING_AN_ENGINE.md): task recipes.
- [Testing](https://github.com/Davidslv/seams/blob/main/doc/reference/TESTING.md): the test model for generated engines.
- [API reference](https://rubydoc.info/gems/seams): YARD docs for the gem's public API.

## Notes

Seams is a code generator: the generated code is the product. When reasoning
about behaviour, read the generator templates under
`lib/generators/seams/**/templates/` — the `.tt` files — not just the gem's
runtime code under `lib/seams/`.
